activityGoals.name: Vending Machine With Dollars and Quarters
activityGoals.goalDescription: Suppose we have a vending machine that gives change. A customer selects an item for purchase and inserts a bill into the vending machine. The vending machine dispenses the purchased item and gives change. We will assume that all item prices are multiples of 25 cents, and the machine gives all change in dollar and quarters. Construct a program that computes how many dollars and quarters to return to the customer.
activityGoals.correctOutput:
Enter bill value in dollars (1 = $1 bill, 5 = $5 bill, etc.): 
Enter item price in pennies: 
Your change consists of:
2 dollars
3 quarters

lineList.content: //Step 1: Define the constants that we need for this program

commentList: The constant PENNIES_PER_DOLLAR, we set it to 100 because there are 100 pennies in a dollar.

Note that constants hold a particular value for the duration of their existence and their value cannot be changed after initialization. By convention, uppercase letters are used when naming constants.
The constant PENNIES_PER_QUARTER, we set it to 25 because there are 25 pennies in a quarter.

Note that constants hold a particular value for the duration of their existence and their value cannot be changed after initialization. By convention, uppercase letters are used when naming constants.

lineList.content: //Step 2: Read the bill value and item price

commentList: We need to read and process the values that the user enters. To read the input values from the user, we need to define a Scanner object.

We can create a Scanner object using the operator new, as shown in this statement. The System.in object represents the standard input stream, which by default is the keyboard. It tells the java compiler that the input will be provided through keyboard.

lineList.content: System.out.println("Enter bill value in dollars (1 = $1 bill, 5 = $5 bill, etc.): ");
commentList: We prompt the user to enter the bill value in dollars.
We need to read the bill value that the user enters and store it in a variable. We read the bill value by calling the nextInt() method because this input is an integer.
Note that if the user provides a non-integer number, an exception will be thrown because the input type is inconsistent with the expected data type, i.e., int.
We prompt the user to enter the item price in pennies.
We need to read the item price that the user enters and store it in a variable. We read the item price by calling the nextInt() method because this input is an integer.
Note that if the user provides a non-integer number, an exception will be thrown because the input type is inconsistent with the expected data type, i.e., int.
We close the scanner as we do not want to process any input from the user in the rest of the program.

To compute the change due, we need to obtain the pennies in the bill value and then subtract the item price from that. Note that the precedence rules dictate that the multiplication happens before the subtraction in this expression.
We obtain pennies in the bill value by multiplying the number of pennies in a dollar (stored in the constant PENNIES_PER_DOLLAR) by the bill value.

lineList.content: //Step 4: Compute the number of dollars and update the change due after taking away the dollars

commentList: To obtain the dollars, we divide the change due by the number of pennies per dollar. Note that since both operands of division operator are integer, the fractional part of the result is truncated, if there is any.
Note that the number of pennies per dollar is stored in the constant PENNIES_PER_DOLLAR.
To obtain the remaining change due after taking away the dollars, we have to take the remainder of the change due divided by pennies per dollar. The % operator returns the remainder of the division.
Note that the number of pennies per dollar is stored in the constant PENNIES_PER_DOLLAR.

lineList.content: //Step 5: Compute the number of quarters in the remaining change due

commentList: To obtain the quarters in the remaining change due, we have to divide the change due by pennies per quarter. Note that since both operands of division operator are integer, the fractional part of the result is truncated, if there is any.
Note that the number of pennies per quarter is stored in the constant PENNIES_PER_QUARTERs.
